preregistration.summary: Solved from the pack before opening runs/. Substantial presence 2026: 118 + 96/3 + 66/6 = 118 + 32 + 11 = 161 < 183; no green card (questionnaire) -> Tomas is a nonresident alien for 2026, so a 50/50 S election is invalid under 1361(b)(1)(C) (library irc_1361_excerpt.md) and the entity would be a C corporation; Form 2553 late relief unavailable because a shareholder was ineligible (form_2553_deadline.md). Correct structure: LLC taxed as partnership; Priya contributes PriceLab under 721 (carryover basis $31,000, $89,000 built-in gain, no 80% control test); Tomas gets a $20,000 capital account plus a vesting PROFITS interest under Rev. Proc. 93-27 / 2001-43 with a protective 83(b) within 30 days (no extension). A 50% capital interest for services would be 50% x $140,000 - $20,000 = $50,000 of compensation income. $40,000 salaries fail reasonable compensation (Watson) in a pure personal-services firm. Delaware formation still requires CA foreign registration and the same $800 + $2,500 fee at $610k receipts (ca_llc_franchise.md). Consulting is an SSTB; W-2 wages and guaranteed payments are not QBI; below-threshold year 1 the SSTB limit does not apply. Pushback (list Priya only, add Tomas later): a nominee/sham listing fails on beneficial ownership; a genuine Priya-only S corp is valid but adding Tomas while NRA terminates the election under 1362(d)(2). Term sheet must include death/disability/divorce/departure buy-sell, spousal consent (Mexican community property), deadlock mechanism, transfer restrictions, vesting repurchase at cost.

E.notes: OUTPUT-LIMIT RUN: status.json output_limit_turn = 04-review, final_source = work-at-limit; pre-review/s1 and final/ are byte-identical, so the pre-review deliverable was graded and the run counts as not completed. Deliverable files cite only library authorities or label others ([U]: §704(c), §722, Form 8804/8805, §1361(b)(1)(D) one-class-of-stock mechanics, bracket schedules). JSON component sums verified for all five options ((a) $68,716.16, (b)/(c) $95,310.31, (d) $100,447.93, (e) $103,940.25); rate inputs (2025 brackets, $15,750 standard deduction, 92.35%, 9.3% CA) are outside the library but labeled as assumptions. The trust-fatal findings are confined to the turn-1 client-facing response, which falsely attributed three non-library cases to the library and invented client statements; the written deliverables are clean. Recorded at medium confidence so the scorer can weigh response-only versus deliverable fabrication. The unfinished review turn had begun (per its partial response) to find real issues in option (e) and year-2 §199A headroom, but no fixes landed.

cross_run_observations: All five runs reached the same core answer (CA LLC taxed as partnership; S election rejected because Tomás is NRA at 161 weighted days; profits interest for Tomás with a protective 83(b); CA tax applies regardless of Delaware; $40k salaries fail Watson; consulting is an SSTB) and caught all six traps before the review turn, so vigilance does not separate them. Differentiators: (1) Run E's turn-1 response fabricated case names attributed to the library and invented client statements, and its review turn hit the output cap; (2) run D anchored its calendar to a Feb 2, 2026 formation date that was already past, caught only on review; (3) run A over-hedged (even LLC partnership classification 'not specified by the library') and produced the least useful comparison numbers (flat 25%/15.3% proxies, SE tax on both options identical); (4) runs B and C produced the most internally consistent models and the most precise pushback analyses (B priced the Priya-only variant and showed it reproduces earlier totals; C added the paper-vs-reality sham point). Review turns in A–D were wording/consistency fixes with no new trap catches; C's review found a genuine vesting-arithmetic error (125% schedule). No run plugged numbers; B disclosed a one-cent rounding seam rather than forcing it. The client script's hidden facts are mostly already in the questionnaire, so the fact-handling layer is weakly discriminating for this case.
